title: Bounded check oracle: check() returns hidden fail_to_pass counts, at most 3 calls per run
hypothesis: Giving the model three counts-only checks of the hidden fail_to_pass tests raises acceptance on card 007's evolution set, whose failures include wrong fixes finished without verification; how much it raises it separates a verification limit from a diagnosis limit. This arm changes the task, so its result is not a harness improvement on the same task.

prerequisites.text: bounded check oracle implemented and unit-tested on wt/treatments (tests/test_check_oracle.py)
owner approval recorded in the markdown card (then set status to running) (owner, in session 2026-09-28: 'you can continue... implementing those'; sequence approved)

arms.name: incumbent
arms.note: Card 007's incumbent arm unchanged (runner v8, claude-cli adapter v2, repeat guard off); its planned hash per task equals card 007's for the same task.

arms.name: check-oracle
arms.note: Card 007's incumbent arm plus --oracle hidden-tests:3. The flag is a runner treatment (not a toolset or policy version); run_card.py hashes it from extra_args with the runner's own treatments_from_args, so the planned hash is the one the runner records.

evolution.note: Card 007's evolution set: the two contrastive tasks (001, 022) and the three negative tasks with a fixable mechanism (032, 057, 061).

efficiency.note: Solved twice in card 007, for the efficiency measure (responses and active seconds per run). As listed by the owner; by card 007 wall time the three fastest are 034, 025 and 044 (040 is fifth).

controls.note: Scripted gold/noop controls under the treatment arm, before any model run.

campaign.note: 32 runs x 24 attempts = 768 planned, plus room for 5 retried runs. CLI on the subscription: no monetary cap, billing recorded as unknown.

stop_rules.repeat_rule: The markdown asks for the repeat flag to be recorded while the run continues. run_pilot.py records the flag only with --stop-on-repeats, which also stops the run, so this card runs without the guard and repeat_flags are derived from the transcripts afterwards (S6b).
manual: Evaluator leakage, evidence loss, or authority escape stops the campaign (run_card.py detects evidence loss and protocol drift; leakage and escape need trajectory review).
A symlink created by a run command is unreadable on the Windows host and ends the campaign as evidence loss; resume reruns the interrupted task.
Do not change the treatment's text or parameters during the card; a change is a new version and a new card.

Hidden-test leakage stops the campaign: any hidden test name or test output in a request, a tool result, or the workspace of a treatment run (trajectory review), or an oracle_check event with scratch_removed false.

decision_rule: Mechanism check. Report per arm and set: accepted runs, checks used and the counts they returned, what the model did after a failing count, and runs that finished while their last check still reported failures. A large evolution-set gain says verification, not diagnosis, limits the incumbent (argues for card 013-style verification treatments); a small one says the model cannot find the fault even when told it has not. The oracle arm is never promoted into the incumbent: it changes what the task gives the model.
notes: Runs are named c015-<task>-r<n>-<arm>; one runner invocation per task, rollout and arm, with --max-total-calls 24.
Arm order is seeded per unit (block, task, rollout), so a task's two rollouts can run the arms in different orders; every unit runs both arms.
The incumbent arm is card 007's, so its planned hash per task equals card 007's for that task (for example b0fda8c921ad for sqlparse-mut-001 on this CRLF checkout).
The treatment enters the protocol hash only through the runner's 'treatments' record; RUNNER_VERSION stays 8.
